rows.text: returns `r8` unchanged when `rdx` equals `rcx`; otherwise steps the source `rdx` and the destination `r8` back by 0x230 bytes per element until the source reaches `rcx`, copying each element's dwords `+0` and `+4` and its 0x100 bytes at `+8` (0x80 two-byte steps) and then calling `001C22A0(destination + 0x108, source + 0x108)`; returns the last destination pointer
copies dwords `+0` and `+4` of `rdx` to `rcx` and the 0x100 bytes at `rdx+8` to `rcx+8` (0x80 two-byte steps), then calls `001C22A0(rcx + 0x108, rdx + 0x108)` and returns `rcx`

builds a stack record (dword 0, dword `02CF82A8`, qword `rcx`, byte 1) and, for each block in the chain starting at `02CF8270` and linked through qword `+0x78`, walks the ring headed at the block's `+0x80` forward through qword `+0` of each link, stopping at the head or a null link and calling `0063CE80(&record, link - 8)` for each link while `link - 8` is non-null

builds a stack record (dword 0, dword `02CF84A8`, qword `rcx + 0x30`, or 0 when `rcx` is null, byte 1) and, for each block in the chain starting at `02CF8470` and linked through qword `+0x78`, walks the ring headed at the block's `+0x80` forward through qword `+0` of each link, stopping at the head or a null link and calling `0063CE80(&record, link - 8)` for each link while `link - 8` is non-null

builds a stack record (dword 0, dword `02CF82A8`, qword `rcx`, byte 0) and, for each block in the chain starting at `02CF8270` and linked through qword `+0x78`, walks the ring headed at the block's `+0x80` backward through qword `+8` of each link, stopping at the head or a null link and calling `0063CE80(&record, link - 8)` for each link while `link - 8` is non-null

builds a stack record (dword 0, dword `02CF84A8`, qword `rcx + 0x30`, or 0 when `rcx` is null, byte 0) and, for each block in the chain starting at `02CF8470` and linked through qword `+0x78`, walks the ring headed at the block's `+0x80` backward through qword `+8` of each link, stopping at the head or a null link and calling `0063CE80(&record, link - 8)` for each link while `link - 8` is non-null

notes: 006305A0/006306E0 follow the first link qword at the head (+0x80+0) and each link's qword +0; 00630BE0/00630D20 follow head +0x88 and each link's qword +8, so 'forward'/'backward' only names which link qword is followed. None of the four ring walkers sets a return value, so no return is stated.
